One air force.
Many different roles.

Explore six common air force aircraft roles—from fighters and bombers to the aircraft that transport, refuel, observe, and train.

01 / AIR DEFENSE & MULTIROLE

Fighter aircraft

Air defense & multirole

Fast, maneuverable aircraft designed for air defense. Multirole fighters can also perform other combat missions.

02 / LONG-RANGE STRIKE

Bomber aircraft

Long-range strike

Aircraft designed primarily to carry and deliver weapons against surface targets, often emphasizing range and payload.

03 / AIRLIFT & LOGISTICS

Military transport

Airlift & logistics

Aircraft that carry personnel, equipment, and supplies, including support for disaster relief and medical transport.

04 / EXTENDING FLIGHT ENDURANCE

Aerial refueling tanker

Extending flight endurance

Aircraft equipped to transfer fuel to compatible aircraft in flight, allowing them to remain airborne longer.

05 / SEEING THE BIGGER PICTURE

Surveillance & early warning

Seeing the bigger picture

Aircraft equipped with sensors and communications systems to observe activity and support a shared picture of the airspace.

06 / DEVELOPING FLYING SKILLS

Trainer aircraft

Developing flying skills

Aircraft used to teach pilots, from foundational handling to more advanced flight and aircraft systems.
